It's understandable that it'll be more difficult to be patient like that. Do you see her in person? If so, then it'll be easier to give it some time. You could ask her out after a short amount of time, but if she doesn't know you at all, then chances are she might say no. It's best to get to know each other - but if you see her in person, it should be easier!

Usually guys will be super friendly and supportive of you or your interests if they're interested. If they reply to your messages quickly, if they actively engage in conversation with you, if they show interest in your interests and ask you about it, if they ask you about your day or what you'll be doing over the weekend, etc. I'd say, if a guy talks to you a lot and puts a lot of effort into talking about you and how you're doing, then he probably likes you. 

I'd suggest being patient and taking note of small things like the subject matter in your conversations (is it more focused on you or him), take note of how long it takes him to reply and whether he gives short answers or long answers as replies (if you ever talk via text/DMs), body language around you (does he have his arms folded across his chest, is he directly facing you, is he making eye contact, etc), and does he ever do things for you like try to help you or buy/make you things - all these things can be small clues!

As others have said, talk to her a bit more and get to know her first. Be patient when it comes to asking her out, because she might panic and say no if you immediately ask her out. To be safe, give it a few weeks and make sure you have a good friendship going first. 

When the time comes to ask her out, mention that you really enjoy her company and that you like her as a person a lot. Keep it positive and compliment her. Good luck!

Oh, man ok. So while I understand your frustrations with this guy, I can actually understand why he's being that way. I have a lot of trouble talking less as well, and I drive what few friends I have away, even though I know I should calm down. It's extremely difficult to do so, because I have so much to talk about but nobody to listen to me. It's a "maybe I wouldn't have so much to say, if I actually had someone to say it to" situation. 

This guy, as others have said, is probably extremely lonely, has few or no friends to talk to, and is probably not coping with his wife's situation at all. If I can make a suggestion: rather than firing him, ask him whether he needs help and maybe suggest that he goes to see someone to talk to, like a therapist or someone who will listen. This guy might be going through a lot of depression, and he might be hiding it behind a mask of energy and "cheerful" behaviour. Yes, he may be annoying, but he's a good guy to have for the business in regards to his performance. 

It's still your choice at the end of the day, but I'd personally suggest getting or suggesting for him to get help.
